title: ckpt-format sandbox + quick repro notes
content:
Quick context:
- Sandbox run: tried to bring up customer-prod v1.2 weights (name: oakley-13b-raw) locally via gcs staging mirror. Getting loader failures in our Tensor/deserialize path.
- Symptoms: immediate crash at model.load_state_dict: "unexpected key 'transformer.h.256.attn.k_proj.weight'" and later a ValueError: "Missing shard file: shard_07.pt (expected 8 shards)" depending on which attempt.

Notes / raw commands I ran (iterative, messy):
1) inspect tarball/objects on GCS
   gsutil ls -l gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/ | tail -n 40
   gsutil cp gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/checkpoint.tar.gz ./ckpt.tar.gz && tar -tf ckpt.tar.gz | head -n 50
   -> tar listing seemed to show 7 shard files + manifest.json.gz (manifest size 1.2k)

2) manifest checks
   gzcat manifest.json.gz | jq .
   -> manifest.shards = 8, manifest.format = "redwood-ckpt-v1"
   -> one shard file name listed: shard_07.pt but not present in tar listing -> mismatch at source (likely broken upload)

3) direct object listing vs composition metadata (weird):
   gsutil stat gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/shard_07.pt
   -> NOT_FOUND
   gsutil ls -L gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b | grep -A2 shard_07.pt
   -> nothing
   BUT storage console shows object but content-encoding: gzip. Suspect double-compressed object or wrong content-encoding metadata set during upstream publish.

4) local load attempts (python snippets):
   # loader quick probe
   import torch, json, gzip
   with gzip.open('manifest.json.gz','rt') as f: m = json.load(f); print(m['shards'])
   shards = [open('shard_%02d.pt','rb').read(16) for i in range(m['shards'])]  # fails for missing file

   # map_location to cpu to avoid CUDA noise
   torch.load('shard_00.pt', map_location='cpu')
   -> raises EOFError: Ran out of input (file seems truncated)

5) downloaded single shard via browser from storage console (the object that shows up in console). Downloaded file size: 12.4MB. Running file(1) shows "gzip compressed data". Running gzip -d produced a .pt that is 512MB. Loading that with torch.load works => indicates uploaded object had content-encoding gzip but was also stored gzipped raw. When gsutil cp downloads, by default it automatically ungzips if content-encoding header present? There may be double-encoding or a mismatch between how we publish (composer job that sets metadata) and how we expect shards to be laid out.

6) another strange case: downstream loader sometimes sees format "redwood-ckpt-v1" and uses legacy shard naming (shard_0..shard_7) while manifest contains zero-padded names (shard_00..shard_07) -> loader mismatch on normalization layer. Added fallback to try both naming conventions locally and it allowed load to proceed further.

Error snippets captured: (raw)
- RuntimeError: unexpected key(s) in state_dict: 'transformer.h.256.attn.k_proj.weight'
- ValueError: Missing shard 07 of 8 (expected 8 shards but found 7)
- EOFError: Ran out of input (for torch.load of shard file)
- OSError: archive header is corrupt (when downstream code attempted tarfile.open on ckpt.tar.gz)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Publishing pipeline (composer job) set content-encoding=gzip and also stored gzipped file -> clients that respect content-encoding get double-unzipped or no unzip depending on client (gsutil behavior differs vs storage console download). Leads to truncated/incorrect length on some readers.
2) Manifest generation bug: mismatched zero-padding and naming reconciliation (v1 manifest generator mixes formats when migrating older pkgs). Loader expects normalized names. 75% reproduction on files produced by older bake pipeline.
3) Partial upload due to interrupted compose/concatenate job (manifest lists final shards but object for shard_07 didn't exist at publish time).
4) Corruption during archive step: tar/gzip pipeline occasionally truncates last shard if process sees EPIPE from remote writer. Less likely (we saw file present and gzipped).

What I tried to mitigate locally: 
- brute-force download each shard with gsutil -Z (preserve) vs without -Z, try Content-Encoding toggles via gsutil setmeta (can't set on object we don't own in customer bucket).
- local fallback loader that tries: exact manifest name -> fallback zero-padding -> strip .gz unwrap and then torch.load with fallback for EOF (retry read)
- small script to detect double-compressed objects: read first bytes, if magic == 0x1f8b (gzip) then run gzip to decompress; re-run torch.load; if torch.load fails with EOF then try streaming decompress with zlib detect.
- created a small repro: pack a 3-shard ckpt but set manifest.shards=4 and publish to staging; loader reproduces Missing shard error.

Next steps / TODOs: 
- Ask storage team to verify content-encoding metadata for namespace gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/ (ticket created: INF-6789).
- Update publish pipeline to ensure we consistently use uncompressed objects and leave gzip Content-Encoding only for HTTP-serving paths (or vice versa — decide one canonical approach).
- Harden loader: on MissingShard, attempt to check object metadata via storage API; if content-encoding present, try both behaviors before aborting. Add clear actionable error message that includes storage object metadata so ops can triage quickly.
- Add a small validation step in CI of publish pipeline that compares manifest.shards vs actual objects list and fails the job early.
- Re-run end-to-end with corrected shard_07 object (once storage team fixes) and capture final stacktrace.

Notes for handoff to SRE/storage:
- sample objects: gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/shard_00.pt (exists), shard_01.pt (exists), shard_07.pt (shows in console but gsutil stat 404).
- timestamps: published 2025-02-09 22:13 UTC by composer-job publish-v2 (check run: build-1221).
- manifest path: gs://rwi-models/oakley-13b/manifest.json.gz (md5: 9b2f3c...)
- approx reproduction command (local):
   ./scripts/load_ckpt_probe.py --manifest manifest.json.gz --prefix ./staging/oakley-13b/ --verify-shards

Open questions / things I wanted to try but ran out of time:
- Try curl vs gsutil vs storage api download to see different behaviors for Content-Encoding for the problematic object.
- Check our upload codepath for objects: do we call gzip.compress and then gsutil cp (which might set Content-Encoding automatically) or do we upload raw compressed bytes and also set header? There are two different publishers (legacy bake and new composer) in the same pipeline.
- Is there a manifest v2 spec we should switch to that contains per-shard object metadata (md5/size) to validate at publish time?

Quick helper snippets (save these somewhere else later):
- detect gzip magic: head -c 2 shard_00.pt | od -An -t x1
- verify trailing bytes: tail -c 16 shard_00.pt | xxd
- simple python probe (rough):
   import sys, gzip, torch
   p = sys.argv[1]
   with open(p,'rb') as f:
       sig = f.read(2)
       f.seek(0)
       if sig == b'\\x1f\\x8b':
           import subprocess
           subprocess.check_call(['gzip','-d','-c',p], stdout=open(p+'.decompressed','wb'))
           print('decompressed to', p+'.decompressed')
       else:
           print('not gz')

If anyone picks this up: start by checking storage metadata and manifest/object list. I can re-run repro (I saved staging artifacts under /tmp/oakley-debug-20250211).
